title: Sky-pooler cutover leaves index-4 unmintable: newPooler._minter never set to NFTMinterV2, mint(4) reverts
description: DispatcherReplaceSkyPoolerAtIndex4 deploys a fresh BalancerPoolerV2 (step 4) and re-points configs[4].dispatcher to it (step 13), but never calls newPooler.setMinter(NFT_MINTER_V2). ATokenDispatcherV2._minter therefore stays address(0). NFTMinterV2.mint(4) (line 191) calls dispatcher.dispatch(...), whose onlyMinter modifier (ATokenDispatcherV2 line 44-47) requires msg.sender == _minter. With _minter==0 this require fails for every caller. The predecessor cutover (DispatcherReplaceAtIndex4, Story 048) had this exact gap and shipped a dedicated back-fill script SetMinterOnIndex4Pooler.s.sol to call setMinter(NFT_MINTER_V2) on the new pooler; this Story-056 script reintroduces the omission for the Sky pooler and provides no equivalent step. The phUSD-level setMinter calls in the script (steps 6/14) are a DIFFERENT authorization (FlaxToken minter mapping) and do not satisfy the dispatcher's _minter check.
impact: After the cutover, NFT minting at index 4 is fully bricked: every user mint(4) reverts with 'ATokenDispatcherV2: caller is not minter'. The entire stated purpose of the script (keep index 4 mintable via the new Sky-route pooler, NFT id unchanged) is defeated. Requires a follow-up owner transaction (newPooler.setMinter) to recover; until then index-4 is a denial of the primary product function.
evidence: VERIFIED on mainnet fork (block 25241930). Dry preview completes with ALL the script's own asserts passing while leaving _minter=0. test/AuditSkyPoolerMintIndex4.t.sol::test_mint4_reverts_after_cutover_alone runs the full cutover then mint(4) and reverts with exactly 'ATokenDispatcherV2: caller is not minter'. Companion test_mint4_succeeds_once_setMinter_applied applies newPooler.setMinter(NFT_MINTER_V2) and mint(4) then mints 1 NFT — proving the missing call is the sole root cause. Storage proof: old pooler 0x26F8…b38A slot1 (_minter) == 0x39Af…2e10f (NFTMinterV2), set by SetMinterOnIndex4Pooler; a fresh pooler starts at 0. Cluster: script/SetMinterOnIndex4Pooler.s.sol exists for precisely this step.
recommendation: Add a step that calls BalancerPoolerV2(newPooler).setMinter(NFT_MINTER_V2) (owner-only) before or alongside replaceDispatcher(4,newPooler), and add a post-condition smoke test that mint(4) succeeds (or at minimum assert a non-zero _minter via a getter) so the script refuses to declare success while index 4 is unmintable.

title: Script self-spec omits a mint(4) post-condition; all internal asserts pass on a non-functional cutover
description: The script's declared post-conditions (step 16) verify configs(4)==newPooler, hook rotation, BPT migration and sUSDS drain, but never verify the one property the cutover exists to preserve: that mint(4) is callable. Because of this, the PREVIEW path returns 'Script ran successfully' and 'All post-state invariants hold' even though index-4 minting is bricked (see High finding). A dry run that is supposed to fail-fast on misconfiguration gives a false green.
impact: The preview/dry mode — the operator's primary pre-broadcast safety check — does not surface the most important defect. The operator can broadcast in good faith and only discover the break when the first user mint reverts in production.
evidence: Fork dry run at block 25241930 prints 'All post-state invariants hold' while _minter==0 (verified break, see High). No require/assert in run() touches mint(4) or _minter.
recommendation: Extend step 16 with an explicit dispatcher-authorization invariant (e.g. require(newPooler returns NFT_MINTER_V2 as its minter)) and, in PREVIEW mode, a simulated mint(4) smoke test as the manual Sky-route validation already does for the donation path.

title: Broadcast uses --skip-simulation with an offline-derived stale-able minBPT; no live re-query enforced
description: The broadcast variant passes --skip-simulation because the router queryAddLiquidityUnbalanced quote can only run from a true eth_call frame. minBPT is supplied from DEFAULT_MIN_BPT=284e18 (or MIN_BPT_WEI env), derived offline on 2026-06-04 for a ~527.71 sUSDS seed. The seed amount is read live (remaining sUSDS after the 10% redeem), so if pool composition or the seed size moves materially before broadcast, a too-high stale minBPT reverts pool() (failing the whole cutover after irreversible state changes in steps 3-14 have broadcast), while a too-low one weakens slippage protection. --skip-simulation means neither is caught by forge before sending. The script enforces only minBPT>0 and a >=minBPT post-check; it cannot self-detect a stale-too-high floor.
impact: Operational: a stale minBPT can abort pool() at broadcast time after the dispatcher has already been re-pointed and funds swept, leaving a half-applied cutover that needs manual repair; or, if set too low, exposes the single LP add to sandwich/slippage. Bounded by the owner-only, one-shot nature and the operator instruction to re-query.
evidence: Fork at block 25241930: seed 527.80 sUSDS, pool() minted 287.9 BPT vs 284e18 floor (~1.4% margin held). Verified the floor is live-sensitive; staleness risk is real but currently within margin.
recommendation: Before broadcast, re-run the documented cast queryAddLiquidityUnbalanced for the actual current seed and set MIN_BPT_WEI explicitly; consider splitting pool() into its own follow-up transaction so a minBPT failure does not strand a partially-applied dispatcher cutover.

title: Broadcast access control hinges on Ledger HD m/44'/60'/46'/0/0 deriving the owner; unverifiable from script
description: Every mutating call in the broadcast path is onlyOwner (NFTStaker.pullAndRefresh/setDispatcherHook, NFTMinterV2.replaceDispatcher, PHUSD.setMinter, oldPooler.withdrawBPT/rescueERC20, newPooler setters). The broadcast is signed by the Ledger at HD index 46 (m/44'/60'/46'/0/0). The script asserts owner==OWNER_ADDRESS (0xCad1…D0B6) but cannot assert that the Ledger derivation yields that address.
impact: If the physical Ledger at index 46 does not derive 0xCad1…D0B6, the broadcast reverts on the first onlyOwner call (pullAndRefresh) — a wasted/failed broadcast, no fund loss. Low because it fails closed and matches the HD index used by sibling Story-048 scripts.
evidence: Live: NFTStaker.owner()==NFTMinterV2.owner()==PHUSD.owner()==oldPooler.owner()==0xCad1…D0B6. HD-path derivation not verifiable without the device.
recommendation: Operator should confirm the address shown by the Ledger under m/44'/60'/46'/0/0 equals 0xCad1…D0B6 before broadcasting (forge prints the derived signer; abort if mismatched).
